title: They Burned 1,200 Acres in 45 Minutes. On Purpose.
description:
Why do firefighters set a forest on fire on purpose? At Fort Stewart, Georgia, a helicopter drops small ignition balls over the longleaf pines and more than 1,200 acres burn in about 45 minutes, a controlled prescribed burn. NASA's FireSense project turned this burn into an experiment: three aircraft, four sensors and the AVIRIS-3 imaging spectrometer tracked the fire while it was still burning.

In this episode:
0:00 Ignition balls over Georgia
0:19 Fort Stewart and prescribed fire
0:58 NASA FireSense: the experiment
1:20 The helicopter and the sphere dispenser
1:50 Three planes, four sensors, AVIRIS-3
2:26 Satellites vs aircraft
2:42 Why these forests need fire
